name: Should I use wood or PVC trim for bathroom finish carpentry?

mainEntity.name: Should I use wood or PVC trim for bathroom finish carpentry?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard MDF and unsealed pine absorb moisture rapidly, leading to swelling, peeling paint, and joint separation in humid bathrooms. Finish carpenters typically recommend water-resistant materials such as PVC, poly-ash trim, cellular PVC, or properly sealed decay-resistant hardwoods for high-moisture zones. In well-ventilated powder rooms or areas away from showers, premium finger-jointed poplar or sealed pine can work, provided all end cuts and rear faces are primed and caulked prior to installation.
acceptedAnswer.description: PVC or moisture-resistant composites are best near showers and tubs because they will not warp or swell, while sealed wood is suitable for drier areas or powder rooms.
